p: Hemel Hempstead is a bit of a winter sports town on the quiet. As well as the rink, The Snow Centre is also in Hemel, so if your lot have caught the bug for sliding about, you could pair a skating session with a go on real indoor snow another day. It's a fun way to turn a single outing into a little winter-themed weekend, whatever the actual season.

For the skating itself, the golden rule is dress warm but light. A rink is chilly, but you'll warm up quickly once you're moving, so layers you can peel off are ideal. Gloves are a must, and long socks stop hire boots rubbing. Leave scarves tucked in rather than flapping about.

First-timers should start slow and stay near the barrier until they find their balance. Bend the knees, keep your weight over your feet and take small steps to begin with. If you start to fall, try to go down sideways and keep your hands tucked in. Then get back up quickly, because the ice is busy and nobody wants to trip over you.

Outside the rink, Hemel has more to offer than many people realise. Gadebridge Park is a large, leafy green space close to the old town, with play areas and room for the kids to run off any remaining energy. The old town High Street itself has a much more traditional feel than the newer centre, with independent shops and places to eat, so it's a nice spot for a stroll and a bite after your session.
